author: WP01
summary: A registry of the 25 public renderer identities with family and platform gate, five implementation classes, a coarse P/T/N/Q capability-and-evidence matrix, operation-level questions and evidence rules. Synchronised for d6e9ff05 and current at TARGET. The site's renderer reference already has a code-derived per-identity capability matrix and a per-family evidence table, which supersede the coarse matrix; the implementation classes, operation checklist and evidence rules were missing and are on the compatibility and evidence page.

concepts.text: CNA exposes 25 public renderer identities over 21 implementation families; the five GL profiles share EasyGL and every other identity has its own family.
Each selector maps to a family and a principal target or platform gate (for example WEBGPU through wgpu-native or browser WebGPU, FREEDIRECT through the free-direct dependency, METAL on macOS only).
Defaults are WEBGL2 under Emscripten, OPENGLES3 on Linux and SDL_RENDERER elsewhere, and the default is not a maturity ranking.
CMake can build a compatible set and generate a descriptor table, and runtime selection must happen before the first device.

Implementation classes: programmable GPU (EasyGL, Vulkan, WebGPU, Direct3D 9/11/12, SDL GPU, OpenGL 4, Metal), abstraction library (FNA3D, whose internal driver is not a CNA identity), bounded CPU 3D (Software, PortableGL), 2D (seven identities, where refusing 3D is correct) and validation/no-op (Headless, Stub).

A coarse matrix marks per group whether 2D, 3D, render targets, MRT, custom source, compiled effects and readback are pixel-producing (P), trace-only (T), deliberately absent (N) or need a narrower document (Q).
concepts.note: The site's matrix is per identity, covers all 19 GraphicsCapability members and is derived from each renderer's code, which is stronger than the coarse group symbols.

concepts.text: Evidence ceilings are family-specific: EasyGL and the principal GPU families have renderer pixel suites, DIRECTX9 adds the XNA oracle, Software gives deterministic CPU pixels, Headless stops at validation, Stub proves survival, and browser, native Windows and macOS claims need their host artifact.

Before relying on a capability, check the concrete operation: texture dimension/format/transfer/sampling, target kind, depth, samples, resolve and mips, vertex/index formats and offsets, state objects and caching, effect variant and shader form, query/readback timing and presentation rectangles, and the platform handle and selected descriptor.
tokens: pin down the operation, not the feature name

target.evidence: DirectX9Renderer.cpp (cube faces in a multi-target set refused) as the worked instance

concepts.text: Evidence rules: source and declared capability are prerequisites; renderer-engaged names the family and operation; pixel-verified uses a discriminating image; oracle-compared names reference and tolerance; unsupported, skipped and blocked stay distinct.
A completeness gate compared the 25 registry identities with the appendix in both directions and a private scan required zero former-identity occurrences in the manuscript.
concepts.note: Book production gate; the site's own equivalent is scripts/check_retired_renderers.py.
